# BearSSL, for the console API's https

Upstream: https://www.bearssl.org/ (git https://www.bearssl.org/git/BearSSL),
commit `7bea48e5e850ab4cafbe68d3765cdaba13a86d6f 2026-04-06`. MIT licence (LICENSE.txt). `src/` and `inc/` are copied
unchanged; nothing outside them is used.

Why BearSSL: portable C with no allocation of its own, constant-time, and
small -- written for exactly this class of machine. It does TLS 1.2 (not
1.3), which every console in front of a modern web server still offers.

It learns nothing from the platform on a Mac: `BR_USE_UNIX_TIME` and the
system RNGs are off (Retro68 defines none of the macros that turn them on),
so the agent seeds it from its own RNG and sets the validation time from the
Mac's clock. The trust anchors are `src/core/anchors.c`, generated by
`tools/gen-anchors.py`.
